ref_summary: To access Mozilla Thunderbird conveniently in Ubuntu, users can drag its application icon from Dash Home onto the desktop launcher. Within the application's inbox, bold text distinguishes unread emails, and new messages can be downloaded using the Get Mail option. Messages can be sorted in ascending or descending alphabetical order by clicking column headers like From or Subject. Thunderbird also enables organizing messages using tags such as Important or Work, with important emails highlighted in red. Tags can be removed by reselecting them, and the Quick Filter toolbar provides an option to display only tagged emails. Furthermore, Thunderbird supports message threads, grouping related correspondence into structured conversations. Users can enable threaded view from the corner of the inbox, inspect full conversation histories in the preview panel by clicking the threading symbol, and exit the view by clicking the thread icon again. Finally, emails can be saved into dedicated desktop folders for archiving and printing.

In LibreOffice Impress, a slide background encompasses all colors and graphic effects behind the slide content. Through the Slide Master feature, accessible from the View menu, modifications and formatting preferences can be applied uniformly across an entire presentation. The Master View toolbar allows users to create, delete, and rename master pages. Slide backgrounds can be customized using the Page Setup dialog box under the Format menu or via the right-click context menu, where options such as blank bitmaps or solid colors like Blue 8 can be selected. For optimal readability, text colors should contrast sharply with the background, and they can be modified through the Character dialog box on the Font Effects tab. Furthermore, design elements and basic geometric shapes, such as rectangles, circles, and triangles, can be inserted using the Basic Shapes toolbar at the bottom of the screen. When a shape is drawn, eight control points appear around it, allowing users to resize and adjust the object easily.

The gedit text editor is pre-installed in Ubuntu Linux and can also be installed through the Ubuntu Software Centre. To launch gedit, users can search for it in Dash Home and click the application icon, or alternatively open the terminal using the keyboard shortcut Ctrl + Alt + T, type gedit, and press Enter. The gedit interface features a menu bar, a toolbar containing common tool icons, a central editing area, and a status bar. Newly created files are assigned the default tab name Untitled Document 1. An asterisk appears beside the file name whenever unsaved changes are present. At the bottom, the status bar displays the cursor's line and column numbers alongside the text entry mode, which defaults to insert mode (INS). Users can save files by navigating to the File menu and selecting Save, which removes the unsaved asterisk indicator. Files can be closed through the File menu, and new documents can be opened either via the File menu or the toolbar's plus icon. Existing documents are accessed through File and Open.

Snippets in the gedit text editor are reusable lines of text or source code that prevent repetitive typing during programming. The feature functions as a default plugin in gedit and can be enabled through the Preferences menu under the Edit option. In a C program, typing a trigger word such as "if" followed by the Tab key automatically inserts the full syntax of an if statement with the cursor positioned on the condition. The Snippets manager, accessed via the Tools menu, allows users to view and manage language-specific snippets. For instance, expanding the C section displays snippets like "if" and "else if", which uses "elif" as its tab trigger. In the Manage Snippets window, users can review syntax in the top-right panel and view the associated tab trigger. Furthermore, users can create new custom snippets by selecting the desired language, clicking the plus icon, naming the snippet, and entering the desired code in the edit panel.

To apply custom animations in LibreOffice Impress, open the presentation and select a slide from the slides pane. Select a text box by clicking on its text and border, then navigate to the tasks pane and open the Custom Animation panel. Clicking Add opens the Custom Animation dialog box on the Entrance tab, which governs how objects appear on the slide. Various animation effects, such as Diagonal Squares, Wedge, and Diamond under the Basic category, can be assigned to different text boxes, and their display speeds can be adjusted to Slow or Medium. Added animations are listed chronologically in the animations box and can be previewed using the Play button, either individually or simultaneously by holding the Shift key. Furthermore, double-clicking any listed animation opens the Effect Options dialog box. Users can modify custom properties such as motion direction under the Effects tab or introduce start delays under the Timing tab to refine presentation effects.

Mozilla Thunderbird is a cross-platform email client that allows users to manage multiple email accounts and download messages to a local computer. It supports importing mail folders and address books from services like Gmail, Yahoo, and Eudora. When using POP3, multiple accounts can be combined into a single inbox, and messages can be sorted by criteria such as date, priority, or custom labels. On Ubuntu Linux, Thunderbird can be installed via the Ubuntu Software Center and launched by searching for the application in Dash Home. The interface features a main menu with shortcuts for retrieving mail, composing messages, and opening the address book. It is divided into two panels: the left displays account folders, while the right offers advanced features and account options. To use Thunderbird with external services, POP3 must be enabled, which in Gmail is done under Settings in the Forwarding and POP/IMAP tab before saving changes.

Command line arguments allow inputs to be passed to a program during execution. In a C program, the main function accepts two arguments: argc and argv. The parameter argc represents the total number of command-line arguments, including the program's actual executable name. The parameter argv is an array storing the actual arguments starting at index 0, where index 0 holds the program name, index 1 holds the first passed argument, and index 2 holds the second. To compile the code file main-with-args.c in Ubuntu using the GCC compiler, the command "gcc main-with-args.c -o args" is entered into the terminal. Running the program with "./args" results in an argument count of 1 because the zeroth argument is the executable filename itself, while the first argument is null. When executing the program with additional parameters like "sunday monday tuesday", the total argument count becomes 4, with "sunday" assigned as the first argument, "monday" as the second, and "tuesday" as the third.

Peer review and document tracking in LibreOffice Writer allow multiple contributors to add, modify, or delete text while clearly showing all revisions in the same file. To enable revision tracking, navigate to Edit, select Changes, and enable the Record option, ensuring that the Show option is also active. When text is inserted, it appears in a distinct color, and hovering over it displays the reviewer's name along with the timestamp of the edit. This name is drawn from the user details entered when LibreOffice was installed. Deleting text does not remove it immediately; instead, it marks the content for deletion and identifies who flagged it. LibreOffice Writer visually differentiates revisions by assigning unique colors to edits made by different reviewers. Hovering over any altered text identifies who performed the modification. Multiple users can thus collaborate, review each other's additions and removals across shared documents, and accept or reject edits before finalizing the document.

LibreOffice Writer provides multiple view options to display documents according to different needs. The Print Layout option displays the document as it will appear when printed, whereas Web Layout displays it as it would appear in a web browser, making it ideal for creating HTML documents. Users can access Full Screen mode through the View menu to edit documents or present them on a projector, and press the Escape key to exit. To adjust page magnification, the Zoom option in the View menu opens the Zoom and View Layout dialog box. Within this dialog, Zoom Factor includes settings such as Optimal, Fit width and height, Fit to width, 100% view, and a Variable field for custom zoom percentages. Furthermore, the View Layout section allows users to display pages sequentially one below another using Single page, or side by side using the Automatic option. Document view layouts and zoom can also be quickly adjusted using controls on the Writer status bar, including single column and book modes.

The LibreOffice Impress interface consists of a central workspace with five view buttons: Normal, Outline, Notes, Handout, and Slide Sorter. The Slides pane on the left displays slide thumbnails, while the Tasks pane on the right includes presentation layouts. Users can insert a new blank slide by selecting an existing slide in the Slides pane and clicking Insert followed by Slide. Slide titles can be added by typing directly into the designated title text box. Impress provides two methods to duplicate slides: using the Duplicate Slide command from the Insert menu or copying and pasting slides in Slide Sorter view using the context menu. For text formatting, users can adjust font family and size using the Text Format toolbar or through the Character dialog box accessed from the Format menu. Additionally, text color can be customized using the drop-down arrow next to the font color icon, and standard text styles such as bold, italics, and underline can be applied via their respective toolbar icons.

LibreOffice Impress is a free, open-source presentation software equivalent to Microsoft Office PowerPoint, compatible with Windows and GNU/Linux operating systems. When installing via package management, the complete option should be selected. Impress can be launched through the Applications menu under Office, either directly or via the main LibreOffice startup dialog by choosing the presentation component. The Impress interface includes title, menu, standard, formatting, and status toolbars. Users can create a presentation from a template by selecting an option such as Recommendation of a Strategy, choosing slide designs like Presentation Backgrounds with a Blue Border, setting the output medium to Original, and specifying presenter details and presentation subjects. The default headings provided in the wizard can be retained to generate the slides. Finally, presentations are saved by selecting File and Save, which defaults to the Open Document Format with the .odp file extension, and can be reopened later from the File menu.

To launch JChemPaint, open the terminal using Ctrl + Alt + T, navigate to the desktop directory, and execute the application jar file with Java. The lower toolbar provides quick-access element buttons alongside options to select elements from the periodic table or enter symbols via the keyboard. Opening the periodic table launches a window where hovering over an element, such as oxygen, displays its properties in an information box. Alternatively, choosing the keyboard input option allows users to type an element symbol like Xe directly onto the canvas. When constructing xenon difluoride, uncheck implicit hydrogens in the preferences window. Single bonds can then be drawn between fluorine and xenon by dragging from the xenon atom when a blue circle appears. Furthermore, right-clicking an atom displays its popup menu, which contains choices for isotopes, molecular properties, and changing the element. For instance, navigating through the alkali earth metals category enables replacing xenon with calcium.

The tutorial demonstrates the use of typedef and union in C programming. The typedef keyword assigns symbolic names or aliases to existing or user-defined data types, enhancing code clarity and ease of modification. Its syntax is demonstrated by defining unsigned int as uint in a palindrome verification program. The program is compiled using gcc and executed via the terminal, successfully confirming a three-digit palindrome input. Next, the tutorial explains the union data type, which is a collection of different data types grouped together. Unlike structures, a union allocates a single shared storage space for all its members, meaning only one member can be accessed at a time. An example code named union.c demonstrates a union called student containing variables for English, Maths, and Science marks. Within the main function, a union variable named stud is declared, its members are accessed to compute total marks, and the compiled program outputs the total as 228.

JChemPaint is a free, open-source, cross-platform 2D chemical structure editor and viewer developed in Java. It enables users to draw chemical structures, configure preferences, and save files with the .mol extension. Furthermore, it supports importing and exporting structural data in plaintext formats such as SMILES, Molfile, CML, and InChIKeys. Running JChemPaint requires Java, which can be installed on Ubuntu through the Synaptic Package Manager. To install JChemPaint on Ubuntu 12.04, the application jar file is downloaded via a browser and moved from the downloads directory to the desktop. Users then launch the application from the terminal by pressing Ctrl+Alt+T, navigating to the desktop directory using the cd command, and executing the java -jar command, as JChemPaint can only be opened through the terminal. For Windows installation, Java SE Runtime Environment 7 must first be obtained by downloading the installer executable from a web browser, accepting the license agreement, and completing the installation wizard prior to setting up JChemPaint.

Mozilla Thunderbird allows users to organise emails by adding custom folders, searching messages with advanced filters, and automating message management through filter rules. In Thunderbird, users can create a new folder, such as "important mails," by right-clicking on an account and selecting the new folder option, allowing emails to be dragged and dropped directly from the inbox. The search messages tool under advanced features enables finding specific messages based on conditions like matching subject text, with options to save search results into a folder. Furthermore, message filters can be established to automatically sort incoming mail; for instance, rules can be defined to detect specific subject keywords and automatically move matching emails to a target folder when run. Thunderbird also supports managing multiple email accounts from providers like Gmail and Yahoo. While Gmail accounts can be configured automatically, accounts such as Yahoo require manual setup after enabling POP access within the account settings.

LibreOffice Writer provides various basic formatting features to enhance plain text documents. Text alignment options include align left, align right, and justify, which distributes text evenly between page margins. Bullets and numbering allow users to distinguish independent points clearly. They are accessed through the Format menu under Bullets and Numbering, where users can select styles from various tabs. Pressing Enter starts a new line with an incremented number or bullet point, and nested bullets or numbers can be created. The Tab and Shift keys increase or decrease bullet indentation levels. Bullets or numbering can be disabled using the Numbering Off option after pressing Enter. Furthermore, repetitive text entry can be avoided using copy and paste functions. Users can select text, right-click to copy, position the cursor, and right-click to paste. Alternatively, keyboard shortcuts Ctrl + C and Ctrl + V can be used for copying and pasting text respectively.

Storage class specifiers in C provide the compiler with crucial information regarding variable storage location, initial values, and variable lifetimes. Their general declaration syntax consists of the storage specifier, followed by the data type and variable name. The auto specifier declares automatic variables, which reside in CPU memory and possess local scope. These variables are not initialized automatically and must be initialized explicitly upon declaration. Attempting to declare an auto variable at file scope outside a function causes a compilation error, specifically indicating that a filescope declaration specifies auto, because auto variables cannot be declared globally. In contrast, static variables are automatically initialized to zero and their storage space is also CPU memory. Unlike automatic variables, static variables retain their values across distinct function calls and are not destroyed when program execution control leaves the enclosing block. Demonstrations illustrate the declaration, compilation, and error handling of auto variables alongside the properties of static variables using Ubuntu Linux and the GCC compiler.

In LibreOffice Impress, presentation notes serve two main purposes: providing additional reference material for the audience on printed handouts and offering cues to guide the presenter during a delivery. To add notes to a slide, select the slide in the slides pane and switch to the Notes tab, where text can be typed into the notes text box beneath the slide. The text within the notes box can be formatted directly by adjusting the font type, changing the font size, and applying bullet points. To maintain consistent formatting across all notes, a Notes Master can be configured via View, Master, and Notes Master. Inside the Notes Master view, modifications made to the notes placeholder—such as altering text size and font color or inserting shapes and logos—automatically apply as defaults to all presentation notes. Finally, the layout can be customized by selecting and moving the slide placeholder, providing additional space to resize the notes placeholder.

In LibreOffice Writer, the Find and Replace feature enables searching for and substituting text across a document. Users can open this tool via the Edit menu or the standard toolbar, input search terms in the Search for field, and enter substitutions in the Replace with field. Selecting Find All highlights every occurrence, while Replace All substitutes every instance immediately. The More Options menu offers specialized search parameters, such as searching backwards from bottom to top, restricting searches to current selections, or using regular expressions and formatting attributes. Additionally, the Spellcheck feature detects spelling errors from the cursor's current position to the end of the text and permits adding unknown words to the user dictionary. Because spell checking varies by language, users configure language preferences through Tools and Options under Language Settings, setting the Western default document language and locale to English USA. Finally, users can enable AutoSpellcheck from the toolbar to automatically identify spelling mistakes while typing.

Newsletters are regular publications with multiple columns that make reading and navigating articles easier. To create a newsletter in LibreOffice Writer, start a new text document and save it. Navigate to Format on the menu bar and select Columns to configure the desired number of columns, their width, spacing, and separator lines. Setting the columns field value to 2 creates two columns in the text area. Text entered fills the first column before automatically moving to the next column. Alternatively, to jump directly to the next column, click Insert, choose Manual Break, select Column break, and click OK. Images can also be inserted and resized to fit within columns. Writer supports various formatting options, including text alignment, highlighting, and setting text background colors. Additionally, banners or advertisements can be created by selecting the Text option from the Drawing toolbar to place a text box. Users can then apply animation effects, such as Blink, to make the text flash.

In LibreOffice Impress, slide shows display presentations on full screens or projectors and cannot be edited during the show. Users can start a slide show using the F5 function key and navigate through slides using keyboard arrow keys, the space bar, or the right-click context menu. Pressing the Escape key or choosing End Show from the context menu exits the presentation. By enabling the mouse pointer visible and mouse pointer as pen options within the Slide Show Settings dialog box, presenters can draw or write directly on slides during a presentation. Slide transitions are visual effects applied when moving from one slide to another. Within the Slide Sorter tab, users can view all slides and easily rearrange their order by dragging and dropping them. Individual slides can have custom transition effects, such as Wipe Up, applied from the Slide Transition section in the Task Pane. Additionally, transition speed can be adjusted to options like medium, and transition sounds can be configured.

To print a presentation in LibreOffice Impress, open the print dialog using the File menu or by pressing Ctrl+P. In the General tab under Document, users can select print formats including slides, handouts, notes, and outline. When printing slides, the LibreOffice Impress tab allows customization of content (such as slide name, date and time, and hidden pages), color settings (original color, grayscale, or black and white), and size options like fitting to a printable page. The Page Layout tab enables printing multiple slides per sheet, choosing the number of slides per page, drawing borders around each page, or printing slides as a brochure for binding. For handouts, the default format places four slides per page ordered left to right and then downwards, with size options disabled. When printing notes typed in the slide's Notes tab, the preview displays the note at the bottom of the slide, and size options in the LibreOffice Impress tab are likewise unavailable.

JChemPaint can be launched from the terminal by navigating to the Desktop directory and running the JAR file using Java. In the JChemPaint window, the panel background color can be customized by opening the Preferences dialog from the Edit menu and selecting the Choose Background Color button. This color picker window provides tabs such as Swatches, HSB, and RGB, with additional tabs like HSL and CMYK available on Windows operating systems. Under the Other Preferences tab, the look and feel of the application window can be altered by choosing from options such as System, Metal, Nimbus, Motif, GTK, or Windows. Additionally, the user interface language can be adjusted; American English is set by default, but other languages like Spanish can be selected, updating both the menu bar and the status bar. Finally, chemical templates can be inserted into the panel by accessing the Templates menu or the side toolbar, where clicking on the All Templates tab reveals the structure templates window with a list of available structures.

LibreOffice Impress provides several view options to create, edit, and organize presentations. By default, Impress opens in Normal view, which is used for creating and editing slides. Users can also change slide designs from the Master Pages section in the Tasks pane. Outline view displays slide contents and headings arranged like a table, allowing presenters to reorganize text items up, down, or across lines. Slide Sorter view enables easy reordering of slides into any desired sequence through simple drag-and-drop operations. Notes view allows presenters to add speaker notes that remain visible on the presenter's monitor during a slideshow while staying hidden from the audience. Finally, the Tasks pane, which can be toggled via the View menu, contains a Layout section for modifying individual slide layouts, such as applying the Content over Content layout. Each view can be accessed either from the View menu or via its dedicated tab.

To create a feedback diagram in Xfig, start by opening the existing block.fig file and saving it under the new name feedback.fig. Grids can be enabled on the canvas to aid drawing. Navigation across the canvas is managed through scroll bars, with current mouse button functions dynamically indicated in the top-right corner. On the vertical scroll bar, the left mouse button moves the canvas up, the right button scrolls down, or the middle button can be dragged to reposition the view vertically. The horizontal scroll bar shifts the view left and right, allowing the drawn block to be centered. To duplicate diagram components, an existing box is copied by selecting it and clicking in the desired position. Text is added using the text tool from the left panel, where the font size can be adjusted to 16, and text justification is set to center alignment. After clicking inside the box, the label "control" is inserted. Finally, directional lines are initiated using the polyline tool with customized arrow modes and arrowheads.
